newsitem.title: UK: LVMH link possible this year - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: LVMH link possible this year - newspaper.

text.p: Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc are prepared to reach a deal this year to combine their drinks businesses with those of French luxury goods group LVMH, said the Financial Times on Thursday.
Quoting John McGrath, chief executive of GrandMet, the article says agreement will be reached only if the benefits are divided fairly among shareholders of the three groups.

On Wednesday LVMH confirmed it had increased its stake in GrandMet to 11.05 percent from 6.4 percent, but reduced its Guinness holding to 12.46 percent from 14.2 percent. The company now holds enough shares in either group to call an emergency general meeting of shareholders.
LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault is seeking to persuade Guinness and GrandMet to drop their proposed 24 billion pound($40.2 billion) merger, to create a group called GMG Brands.

Arnault wants to combine LVMH's brandy and champagne subsidiary Moet Hennessy with the drinks divisions of Guinness and GrandMet to form an 18.6 billion pound group to be listed on the London and Paris bourse. Arnault initially envisaged LVMH should be entitled to a 35 percent stake in this group.
He also wants the remaining food, fast-food and brewing businesses demerged.

The Breton entrepreneur was travelling to London on Thursday to drum up support from institutional investors in the British companies for his plan. Arnault can block the plan outright if he wins the support of enough investors, representing at least 25 percent of GrandMet's capital.
The case for a demerger of the non-drinks businesses was "vigorously rejected" by McGrath, said the newspaper.
"Exhaustive analysis showed, he said, that the parts of the business were not worth more than the whole. If they were GrandMet would have demerged them already," said the article.
But a combination of the three companies' spirits divisions could enhance shareholder value although by a merger within the GMG structure rather than a separately listed company, McGrath told the FT.
An article in the Independent newspaper quotes McGrath as saying GrandMet would consider alternative proposals to split Moet Hennessy into two.

"GrandMet and Guinness would not say no to the idea of acquiring the champagne business of Moet Hennessy and giving up the cognac side. We would also consider giving Mr Arnault a stake in an unquoted business within GMG Brands incorporating Moet Hennessy and our spirits business," the paper quotes McGrath as saying.
McGrath told the Independent, "It is our clear intention to find some form of settlement between the sides. We are completely open minded to options that create value for our shareholders."
Guinness and GrandMet are analysing Arnault's proposals carefully but it seems they are still not acceptable to them, McGrath says in the Independent newspaper article.
